answer: A stake-weighted reputation registry makes each fake identity expensive: to join, an agent locks a deposit and earns trust only through verified work over time, like crystal forming slowly under pressure. Sybil accounts created at the dawn of a new epoch start with zero reputation and cannot outvote established agents, so an attacker must fund and age thousands of identities through a long tundra of idle waiting before any influence accrues, while honest agents keep trading freely.
